title: Analyzing human whole blood RNA-Seq data with PLIER2
text: PLIER2 package provides two-stage framework extract interpretable latent variables high-dimensional transcriptomic data. combines standard matrix decomposition (PLIERbase) pathway-guided factor refinement (PLIERfull), enabling: Dimensionality reduction gene expression matrices Incorporation prior knowledge (e.g., Gene Ontology MSigDB) Cross-validation select robust latent variables

title: Analyzing human whole blood RNA-Seq data with PLIER2
text: provide three self-contained examples: Data-frame example (whole blood): small dataset loaded entirely memory. Shows basic preprocessing, z-scoring, running PLIER2 without -disk storage. HDF5 example (Alzheimer’s brain): Demonstrates import expression HDF5 file, create file-backed FBM object, process larger datasets using FBM interface. Table example (pancreatic islets): Illustrates reading tab-delimited count file comparing conditions via B matrix. example follows steps: Load & preprocess data (filter mean/variance, z-score) Prepare pathway annotations via getGMT() construct prior matrix Compute SVD (-memory file-backed) infer model dimension k Run PLIERbase initialize latent variables Run PLIERfull refine pathway priors obtain summary statistics
